properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 30 at 2:05PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to reach major flood in the next
few hours. The anticipated crest is expected to be between 39 and
39.5 feet. Crest timing has been delayed to early Saturday
morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 30 at 2:20PM MDT until July 30 at 5:15PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* Until 515 PM MDT.

* At 220 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across Cottonwood Wash. Between 0.8 and 1.2 inches of
rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1
hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Thunderstorms producing flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of creeks and streams, highways, and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Cottonwood Wash to Utah Highway 95
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging currents in a matter
of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 5:15 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 5:15 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 30 at 9:42AM EDT until July 30 at 6:30PM EDT by NWS Albany NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Residual flooding caused by leftover runoff from excessive
rainfall.

* WHERE...A portion of east central New York, including the
following counties, Albany, Columbia, Greene and Rensselaer.

* WHEN...Until 630 PM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is still occurring in some areas. A few
roads remain closed due to flooding. Low-water crossings may be
inundated with water and may not be passable. Expect areas of slow
moving or standing water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 934 AM EDT, Residual flooding is still occurring across
parts of the area with a few roads remaining closed.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hudson, Chatham, Nassau, New Baltimore, Ravena, Coxsackie,
Valatie, Athens, Castleton-On-Hudson, Philmont, Kinderhook,
Lorenz Park, Selkirk, Claverack-Red Mills, Coeymans, Ghent,
Stockport, Stuyvesant, Sunnyside and Stuyvesant Falls.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

SMWTBW

The National Weather Service in Ruskin has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Tarpon Springs to Suwannee River FL out 20
NM...
Waters from Tarpon Springs to Suwannee River FL out 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 500 PM EDT.

* At 416 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 23 nm west of Ozello, moving southeast at
10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats, damage
vessels, and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots,
suddenly higher waves, frequent lightning, and heavy
downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
